name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street
description: Tokyo's oldest and most famous temple, with a dramatic giant lantern gate and bustling market street.
station: Asakusa Station (Tokyo Metro Ginza / Toei Asakusa Line, 5-min walk)

name: Shibuya Crossing & Scramble Square
description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — an iconic Tokyo experience, especially vibrant under neon lights at night.
station: Shibuya Station (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro, Hachiko Exit 1-min walk)

name: Akihabara Electric Town
description: The global epicenter of anime, manga, retro gaming, and electronics culture. Multi-floor arcades and figurine shops.
station: Akihabara Station (JR Yamanote / Hibiya Line, Electric Town Exit)

name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art
description: World-renowned immersive digital art museum where light, mirrors, and sound create an infinite wonderland.
station: Kamiyacho Station (Tokyo Metro Hibiya Line, Direct underground link)

name: Tsukiji Outer Market Breakfast
description: Sample fresh toro sushi, tamagoyaki, and grilled scallops at legendary market stalls. Best visited in the morning.
station: Tsukijishijo Station (Toei Oedo Line) or Tsukiji Station (Hibiya Line)

name: Shinjuku Kabukicho Nightlife
description: Tokyo's most electric entertainment district — neon alleys, izakayas, karaoke towers, and famous Golden Gai bars.
station: Shinjuku Station (JR East / Tokyo Metro, East Exit 5-min walk)

name: Harajuku Takeshita Street & Meiji Shrine
description: From Meiji Shrine's forested tranquility to Harajuku's wild kawaii fashion and crepe shops, Tokyo at its most contrastive.
station: Harajuku Station (JR Yamanote Line) or Meiji-jingumae Station

name: Tokyo Tower & Roppongi Hills
description: Iconic red-and-white Eiffel-inspired communications tower offering panoramic views of Tokyo skyline and Mt. Fuji.
station: Akabanebashi Station (Toei Oedo Line, 5-min walk) or Kamiyacho Station

name: Robot & Entertainment Cabaret Show
description: Outrageous LED lasers, robot dancers, and high-energy Japanese pop performance in the heart of Shinjuku.
station: Shinjuku Station (East Exit 5-min walk)

name: Ueno Park & Museums
description: Vast green cultural hub housing Tokyo National Museum, National Science Museum, Shinobazu Lotus Pond, and cherry trees.
station: Ueno Station (JR Yamanote / Tokyo Metro Ginza & Hibiya Lines, Park Exit)

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Thousand Torii Gates
description: Hike through tunnels of thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up sacred Mount Inari. Magical at dawn or dusk.
station: Inari Station (JR Nara Line, 1-min walk from station entrance)

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Monkey Park
description: Walk through soaring emerald bamboo stalks, cross historical Togetsukyo Bridge, and see wild monkeys on Mt. Iwatayama.
station: Saga-Arashiyama Station (JR San-in Line) or Arashiyama (Hankyu/Keifuku)

name: Kinkaku-ji (The Golden Pavilion)
description: Kyoto's crown jewel Zen temple covered entirely in gold leaf, reflecting across Mirror Pond into surrounding gardens.
station: Kyoto City Bus 101 or 205 to Kinkakuji-michi Bus Stop

name: Gion District Evening Stroll
description: Preserved 17th-century geisha entertainment quarter with wooden machiya teahouses, lanterns, and cobblestone lanes.
station: Gion-Shijo Station (Keihan Main Line) or Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station

name: Traditional Matcha Tea Ceremony Experience
description: Participate in an authentic Zen tea ceremony in a 300-year-old preserved wooden townhouse with a master host.
station: Kyoto-Kawaramachi Station (Hankyu Kyoto Line, 4-min walk)

name: Nishiki Market — 'Kyoto's Kitchen'
description: Five-block covered food arcade with over 100 stalls selling Kyoto pickles, yuba tofu, dango, and skewers.
station: Shijo Station (Karassuma Subway) or Karasuma Station (Hankyu Line)

name: Dotonbori Canal & Street Food Tour
description: Osaka's world-famous neon canal. Feast on piping-hot takoyaki octopus balls, okonomiyaki, and kushikatsu under Glico Man.
station: Namba Station (Osaka Metro Midosuji / Nankai Lines, Exit 14, 3-min walk)

name: Universal Studios Japan & Nintendo World
description: Theme park with interactive Super Nintendo World (Mario Kart AR), Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and anime rides.
station: Universal City Station (JR Yumesaki Line from Osaka Station, 12 min)

name: Osaka Castle & Castle Park
description: 16th-century fortress surrounded by massive moats and plum orchards with an 8-story museum and panoramic top deck.
station: Osakajokoen Station (JR Osaka Loop Line) or Morinomiya Station

name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
description: 650-meter covered market filled with vendors grilling giant king crab legs, A5 wagyu beef skewers, and sea urchin.
station: Nippombashi Station (Osaka Metro Sakaisuji / Sennichimae Lines, Exit 10)

name: Peace Memorial Museum & Atomic Dome
description: Profoundly moving UNESCO peace memorial and museum documenting Hiroshima's post-war renaissance as a city of peace.
station: Genbaku-Dome-Mae Tram Stop (Hiroden Tram #2 or #6 from Hiroshima Station)

name: Miyajima Island & Floating Torii Gate
description: Scenic ferry to sacred Itsukushima Shrine to see the iconic floating orange torii gate rising out of the Seto Inland Sea.
station: Miyajimaguchi Station (JR Sanyo Line) + 10-min JR Ferry (covered by JR Pass)

name: Nara Deer Park & Todai-ji Great Buddha
description: Befriend hundreds of bowing sika deer, then enter Todai-ji, one of the world's largest wooden buildings with a giant Buddha.
station: Kintetsu-Nara Station (10-min walk) or JR Nara Station (20-min walk)

name: Hakone Onsen Hot Springs & Ryokan
description: Recharge in natural volcanic mineral waters surrounded by cedar forests, with multi-course Kaiseki dinner and yukata robes.
station: Hakone-Yumoto Station (Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku, 85 min)

name: Lake Ashi Pirate Cruise & Ropeway Mt. Fuji
description: Cruise volcanic Lake Ashi on a scenic boat with views of Mt. Fuji, then ride the ropeway over steaming Owakudani valley.
station: Togendai Station (Hakone Ropeway / Sightseeing Cruise Port)

name: Kenroku-en Garden
description: One of Japan's Three Great Gardens — immaculate landscape design featuring bridges, ponds, ancient pine trees, and teahouses.
station: Kanazawa Station (15 min via Kenrokuen Shuttle Bus)

name: Higashi Chaya Geisha District
description: Traditional wooden geisha teahouse street where you can sample gold leaf ice cream and visit artisan craft workshops.
station: Hashiba-cho Bus Stop (Loop Bus from Kanazawa Station, 10 min)

name: Yatai Riverfront Food Stalls
description: Pull up a stool at Fukuoka's legendary outdoor street stalls along the Nakasu River for tonkotsu ramen, yakitori, and sake.
station: Nakasu-Kawabata Station (Fukuoka Subway Kuko Line, 4-min walk)

name: Sapporo Beer Museum & Star Hall
description: Explore Japan's beer brewing heritage in red-brick historic brewery, followed by fresh draft beer and Jingisukan lamb grill.
station: Higashi-Kuyakusho-Mae Station (Toho Subway Line) or Sapporo Factory Loop Bus

name: Kerama Islands Snorkeling & Coral Reefs
description: Take a high-speed catamaran to tropical Kerama Blue waters to swim alongside wild green sea turtles and vibrant coral.
station: Tomari Port (Naha) High-speed Ferry (50-min ferry ride)

name: Nikko Tosho-gu Shrine Complex
description: Lavish UNESCO shrine complex in giant cedar forest, dedicated to shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu with famous 'Three Wise Monkeys'.
station: Tobu-Nikko Station (Tobu Limited Express from Asakusa, 100 min + 8-min bus)

name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry
description: Fascinating museum displaying textile looms through automated robotics and car production lines.
station: Sako Station (Meitetsu Nagoya Line, 3-min walk)

name: Shinsekai & Tsutenkaku Tower
description: Nostalgic retro entertainment district famed for kushikatsu skewers, vintage arcades, and Tsutenkaku Tower.
station: Ebisucho Station (Sakaisuji Line) or Shin-Imamiya Station (JR Loop Line)

name: Umeda Sky Building Floating Observatory
description: Marvel at 360-degree open-air panoramic views of Osaka skyline from this futuristic bridge connecting two towers.
station: Osaka Station (JR) or Umeda Station (Hankyu / Subway, 9-min walk)

name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple & Higashiyama
description: Famous wooden stage built without nails offering breathtaking views over Kyoto and cherry blossom hills.
station: Kiyomizu-michi Bus Stop (Kyoto City Bus 206) or Kiyomizu-Gojo Station

name: Nijo Castle & Ninomaru Palace
description: Shogun palace known for ornate gilded carvings, extensive gardens, and 'nightingale chirping' security floors.
station: Nijojo-mae Station (Tozai Subway Line, Exit 1)

name: Odori Park & TV Tower
description: Heart of Sapporo with beautiful flowerbeds, seasonal street festivals, and city observation deck.
station: Odori Subway Station (Namboku / Tozai / Toho Lines, Direct Exit)

name: Susukino Ramen Alley & Nightlife
description: Savor authentic Sapporo miso ramen in narrow Ganso Ramen Yokocho alley followed by vibrant Susukino nightlife.
station: Susukino Subway Station (Namboku Line, 3-min walk)

name: Mount Moiwa Ropeway Sunset Views
description: Ride the cable car to experience one of Japan's top three night views sparkling over the Sapporo plain.
station: Ropeway Iriguchi Tram Stop + Free Shuttle to Ropeway Station

name: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium
description: One of the world's largest aquariums featuring massive whale sharks and manta rays in Kuroshio Sea tank.
station: Yanbaru Express Bus or Okinawa Airport Shuttle directly to Aquarium

name: Shurijo Castle Park
description: Historic palace of the Ryukyu Kingdom combining unique Okinawan and Chinese architectural influences.
station: Shuri Station (Yui Rail Monorail from Naha Airport, 15-min walk)

name: Kokusai Dori Shopping & Izakaya
description: The 'Miracle Mile' of Naha packed with tropical souvenir shops, Okinawan soba eateries, and live Sanshin music.
station: Kencho-mae Station or Makishi Station (Yui Rail Monorail)

name: Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine & Umegae Mochi
description: Magnificent Shinto shrine surrounded by 6,000 plum trees, famous for delicious hot grilled rice cakes.
station: Dazaifu Station (Nishitetsu Dazaifu Line, 5-min walk)

name: Canal City Hakata & Ramen Stadium
description: Massive entertainment and shopping complex with musical fountain shows and a stadium with 8 regional ramen shops.
station: Kushida Shrine Station (Nanakuma Line) or Hakata Station (10-min walk)

name: Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village)
description: Multi-floor building with over 20 stalls grilling savory Hiroshima-style layered okonomiyaki noodles.
station: Hatchobori Tram Stop (Hiroden Tram, 3-min walk)

name: Hiroshima Castle & Shukkei-en Garden
description: Reconstructed carp castle and a miniature landscape garden featuring tranquil ponds, tea cottages, and bridges.
station: Kamiyacho-higashi Tram Stop or Shukkeien-mae Tram Stop

name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
description: World-famous circular museum featuring Leandro Erlich's 'Swimming Pool' and interactive installations.
station: Hirosaka / 21st Century Museum Bus Stop from Kanazawa Station

name: Omicho Seafood Market Feast
description: Lively market serving ultra-fresh Sea of Japan sashimi bowls (kaisendon), snow crab, and grilled skewers.
station: Musashigatsuji / Omicho Market Bus Stop (15-min walk from Kanazawa Station)

name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
description: One of Tokyo's largest and most tranquil imperial parks blending Japanese, French, and English landscape styles.
station: Shinjuku-gyoenmae Station (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, Exit 1)

name: Ginza Shopping & Kabuki-za Theater
description: Prestigious shopping avenue with department stores, fine dining, and the iconic classical Kabuki theater.
station: Ginza Station (Ginza/Marunouchi/Hibiya Lines) or Higashi-Ginza Station
